claim: Cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) is a rare neurovascular disease characterized by enlarged and irregular blood vessels that often lead to cerebral hemorrhage.
source: Cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) is a rare neurovascular disease that is characterized by enlarged and irregular blood vessels that often lead to cerebral hemorrhage.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about CCM presented in the abstract, drawing on established medical knowledge about the disease.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in any of three genes (KRIT1, CCM2, and PDCD10/CCM3) result in CCM lesion formation.
source: Loss-of-function mutations to any of three genes results in CCM lesion formation; namely, KRIT1, CCM2, and PDCD10 (CCM3).
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about the genetic basis of CCM.

claim: This study reports the first in-depth single-cell RNA sequencing combined with spatial transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry to characterize brain endothelial cell subclasses in CCM.
source: Here, we report for the first time in-depth single-cell RNA sequencing, combined with spatial transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry, to comprehensively characterize subclasses of brain endothelial cells (ECs) under both normal conditions and after deletion of Pdcd10 (Ccm3) in a mouse model of CCM.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data and methods described in the manuscript.

claim: Arterial endothelial cells are refractory to CCM transformation.
source: Integrated single-cell analysis identifies arterial ECs as refractory to CCM transformation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the single-cell RNA sequencing data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: A subset of angiogenic venous capillary endothelial cells and resident endothelial progenitors appear to be at the origin of CCM lesions.
source: Conversely, a subset of angiogenic venous capillary ECs and respective resident endothelial progenitors appear to be at the origin of CCM lesions.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the integrated analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Endothelial cells are a particularly heterogeneous cell population with distinct structural, phenotypic, and functional properties.
source: Endothelial cells (ECs) are a particularly heterogenous cell population, as they have distinct structural, phenotypic, and functional properties (Kalucka et al., 2020; Vanlandewijck et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Endothelial cells of arteries, veins, and the lymphatic system show high degrees of specialization in their responses to specific hemodynamic and functional requirements.
source: Recent studies have shown that ECs of arteries, veins, and the lymphatic system show high degrees of specialization in their responses to specific hemodynamic and functional requirements (Augustin and Koh, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Microvascular endothelial cells express highly specialized properties in response to specific requirements of different organs.
source: Compared to large-vessel endothelia, this adaptation of microvascular ECs is seen by their expression of highly specialized properties, in terms of their responses to the specific requirements of different organs.
evidence: This statement draws on established scientific knowledge about microvascular endothelial cell specialization.

claim: Brain microcirculation endothelial cells regulate cerebral blood flow, oxygen delivery, and supply of energy metabolites to nerve cells.
source: The main important functions of these vessels relate to the regulation of cerebral blood flow and oxygen delivery, and the supply of energy metabolites to the nerve cells.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about brain microcirculation function.

claim: Dysfunction of the brain vascular system can cause major problems for brain connectivity, synaptic activity, and information processing.
source: Dysfunction of the brain vascular system can cause major problems for brain connectivity, synaptic activity, and information processing (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Brain microcirculation function requires coordinated cross-talk between endothelial cells and other cell types to establish the neurovascular unit.
source: The specialized function of the brain microcirculation requires coordinated and continuous cross-talk between ECs and the other cell types, to thus establish what is known as the 'neurovascular unit' (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Endothelial cells in neurovascular units are surrounded by pericytes and in contact with glia and neurons.
source: ECs are surrounded and embraced by pericytes and they are in contact with the glia (i.e. astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia) and neurons (Armulik et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Endothelial cells in neurovascular units form the blood-brain barrier (BBB) which controls entry of neurotoxic plasma components, inflammatory cells, and pathogens into brain tissue.
source: The ECs in these neurovascular units form the blood–brain barrier (BBB), which strictly controls the entry of neurotoxic plasma components, circulating inflammatory cells, and pathogens into the brain tissue (Iadecola, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Blood-brain barrier cells promote passage of nutrients and essential molecules from blood into brain through multiple specialized transport systems.
source: As well as their control of general vascular permeability, the cells of the BBB promote the passage of nutrients and other essential molecules from the blood into the brain through their expression of multiple highly specialized transport systems (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Blood-brain barrier integrity is regulated through coordinated interactions of endothelial cells with surrounding neural cells, pericytes, and fibroblasts.
source: Thus, the integrity of the BBB is regulated through coordinated and continuous interactions of the ECs with the surrounding neural cells, pericytes, and fibroblasts, which form a favorable environment for the ECs to develop and express their specialized properties.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about BBB regulation.

claim: Several genetic pathologies causing alterations in BBB development and function arise from inactivation of specific genes in neurovascular unit cells.
source: Several genetic pathologies that can cause alterations in the development and function of the BBB arise as a result of inactivation of specific genes in the cells of the neurovascular units.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about genetic pathologies affecting the BBB.

claim: CCM vascular lesions (cavernomas) mostly develop in the central nervous system and retina.
source: CCM vascular lesions, or cavernomas, mostly develop in the central nervous system and the retina.
evidence: This statement is based on established clinical knowledge about CCM.

claim: CCM lesions can frequently bleed, leading to epileptic seizures, focal neurological deficits, and hemorrhagic stroke.
source: These can frequently bleed, which leads to epileptic seizures, focal neurological deficits, and other neurological problems, such as hemorrhagic stroke (Clatterbuck, 2001; Labauge et al., 2007; Rigamonti et al., 1988; Wong et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: CCM occurs in both familial and sporadic forms.
source: CCMs occur in both familial and sporadic forms.
evidence: This statement is based on established clinical knowledge about CCM.

claim: Familial CCM has an overall prevalence of less than 1:10,000.
source: The familial form of CCM has an overall prevalence of less than 1:10,000.
evidence: This statement provides epidemiological data about familial CCM.

claim: Familial CCM is characterized by multiple CCM lesions that increase in number and size through the patient's life, resulting in recurrent cerebral hemorrhage.
source: It is characterized by multiple CCM lesions that increase in number and size through the life of the patient, which results in recurrent cerebral hemorrhage.
evidence: This statement is based on established clinical knowledge about familial CCM.

claim: Familial CCM is due to loss-of-function mutations in any one of three genes: KRIT1 (CCM1), CCM2 (OSM), and PDCD10 (CCM3).
source: Familial CCM is due to loss-of-function mutations in any one of the three genes known as KRIT1 (or CCM1), CCM2 (or OSM), and PDCD10 (or CCM3).
evidence: This statement is based on established genetic knowledge about familial CCM.

claim: The three types of CCM loss-of-function mutations show comparable morphology and specific brain localization.
source: These three types of CCM loss-of-function mutations show comparable morphology and specific brain localization.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about CCM mutations.

claim: Sporadic CCM has a prevalence of about 1:200.
source: Instead, the sporadic form of CCM has relatively high prevalence, of about 1:200, and in the majority of cases, it occurs as a single cavernoma.
evidence: This statement provides epidemiological data about sporadic CCM.

claim: Sporadic CCM occurs as a single cavernoma in the majority of cases.
source: Instead, the sporadic form of CCM has relatively high prevalence, of about 1:200, and in the majority of cases, it occurs as a single cavernoma.
evidence: This statement is based on established clinical knowledge about sporadic CCM.

claim: Sporadic CCM can result in symptoms similar to familial CCM that depend on cavernoma location.
source: Sporadic CCM can also result in a relatively variable set of symptoms, which are similar to familial CCM and depend on the location of the cavernoma (Labauge et al., 2007; Akers et al., 2017; Cavalcanti et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: There is currently no effective pharmacological treatment for CCM patients.
source: At present, to limit disease progression, there remains the need for an effective pharmacological treatment for patients with CCM, as to date, the only curative therapy is lesion eradication by surgical intervention or stereotactic radiosurgery.
evidence: This statement is based on current clinical knowledge about CCM treatment options.

claim: The only curative therapy for CCM is lesion eradication by surgical intervention or stereotactic radiosurgery.
source: At present, to limit disease progression, there remains the need for an effective pharmacological treatment for patients with CCM, as to date, the only curative therapy is lesion eradication by surgical intervention or stereotactic radiosurgery.
evidence: This statement is based on current clinical knowledge about CCM treatment.

claim: Open skull surgery is currently applied to selected symptomatic CCM lesions only because it is highly invasive and can result in significant complications.
source: Open skull surgery is currently applied to selected symptomatic lesions only, as it is highly invasive, and it can result in significant complications, while being accompanied by unproven long-term benefit.
evidence: This statement is based on current clinical knowledge about CCM surgical treatment.

claim: In familial CCM, neither surgery nor radiotherapy can cure multiple lesions throughout the brain and spinal cord.
source: Also, in familial CCM, neither surgery nor radiotherapy can cure multiple lesions throughout the brain and spinal cord.
evidence: This statement is based on current clinical knowledge about familial CCM treatment limitations.

claim: An effective pharmacological therapy for CCM is still missing despite many studies.
source: Therefore, despite many studies into CCM, an effective pharmacological therapy for this disease is still missing (Abdelilah-Seyfried et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Cdh5(PAC)-Cre-ERT2/Ccm3f/f/Cldn5(BAC)-GFP mice were used for endothelial cell-specific recombination.
source: To study the EC subpopulation(s) that form lesions in CCM, we used Cdh5(PAC)-Cre-ERT2/Ccm3f/f/Cldn5(BAC)-GFP mice for EC-specific recombination (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental mouse model used in the study.

claim: Following a single tamoxifen injection at P1, Cdh5(PAC)-Cre-ERT2/Ccm3f/f/Cldn5(BAC)-GFP mice develop CCM lesions in the brain by P8 that resemble human cavernomas.
source: Following a single tamoxifen injection administered to the pups on their first day after birth, by P8 these mice develop CCM lesions in the brain that resemble human cavernomas (Figure 1A–C; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data and images showing CCM lesion development.

claim: Endothelial cells were isolated and enriched (CD45- and CD31+) from brains of both Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko littermates for droplet-based scRNA-seq.
source: ECs were isolated and enriched (CD45- and CD31+) from the brain of both Cre-negative (Pdcd10-wt) and Cre-positive (Pdcd10-ko) littermates and processed for droplet-based scRNA-seq.
evidence: This statement describes the experimental methods used for cell isolation and sequencing.

claim: ScRNA-seq libraries were prepared using the 10× Genomics platform.
source: ScRNA-seq libraries were prepared using the 10× Genomics platform, and the R toolkit Seurat (version 3) (see Materials and methods) was used for integrated data analysis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental methods used for library preparation.

claim: The R toolkit Seurat (version 3) was used for integrated data analysis.
source: ScRNA-seq libraries were prepared using the 10× Genomics platform, and the R toolkit Seurat (version 3) (see Materials and methods) was used for integrated data analysis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the computational methods used for data analysis.

claim: After quality control, 15,057 cells from two Pdcd10-wt mice and 17,204 cells from two Pdcd10-ko mice were analyzed jointly.
source: After quality control, 15,057 cells from two Pdcd10-wt mice and 17,204 cells from two Pdcd10-ko mice were analyzed jointly.
evidence: This statement provides quantitative data about the number of cells analyzed.

claim: Through unsupervised clustering, 17 cell clusters were distinguished and visualized using UMAP.
source: Through unsupervised clustering, 17 cell clusters (C) were distinguished and visualized using 'uniform manifold approximation and projection' (UMAP) (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This statement describes the results of the clustering analysis, supported by figures.

claim: Four clusters were identified as mixed with non-endothelial cells (C10, C11, C15, C16).
source: Based on the expression of a panel of known brain endothelial marker genes (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B), four clusters were identified as mixed with non-ECs (C10, C11, C15, C16).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of marker gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: Two clusters were identified as enriched in pericytes (C11) and microglia (C16).
source: While the identity of C15 remains unclear, two clusters were identified as enriched in pericytes (C11) and microglia (C16) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of marker gene expression patterns.

claim: Cluster 10 appeared to be a mixture of endothelial cells and astrocytes.
source: Cluster 10 (C10), instead, appeared to be a mixture of ECs and astrocytes, as marker genes of both of these cell types were highly expressed in this population (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of marker gene expression patterns.

claim: The remaining 13 endothelial subpopulations were categorized into six groups: venous, arterial, capillary, tip, mitotic/capillary, and tip/capillary cells.
source: The remaining 13 endothelial subpopulations were then characterized on the basis of the overall expression levels of the reported endothelial marker genes (Figure 1H,I; Supplementary file 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2E). These were categorized into six groups of ECs, as venous (C9), arterial (C8), capillary (C0, C3, C4, C5), tip (C1, C6), mitotic/capillary (C2, C7), and tip/capillary (C12, C13, C14) cells (Figure 1H,J).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of marker gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: Capillary endothelial cells were further distinguished into venous (C2, C4, C7) and arterial (C3, C5) subtypes.
source: The capillary ECs were further distinguished into venous (C2, C4, C7) and arterial (C3, C5) (Figure 1I,J; Sabbagh et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of marker gene expression patterns and supported by a citation.

claim: All endothelial subpopulations except C13 showed significant down-regulation of Pdcd10 expression after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: All of the endothelial subpopulations except C13 showed significant down-regulation of Pdcd10 expression after Pdcd10 deletion (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of gene expression data shown in a figure.

claim: The mixed endothelial and non-endothelial cell clusters (C10, C11, C15, C16) did not show Pdcd10 down-regulation.
source: As expected, the mixed endothelial and non-EC clusters (C10, C11, C15, C16) did not show Pdcd10 down-regulation.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of gene expression data.

claim: Venous/venous capillary endothelial cells in C9 were highly modified by Pdcd10 deletion.
source: The comparisons between the total numbers of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) indicated that the venous/venous capillary ECs in C9 were highly modified by Pdcd10 deletion, while the arterial ECs in C8 were essentially not affected (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Arterial endothelial cells in C8 were essentially not affected by Pdcd10 deletion.
source: The comparisons between the total numbers of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) indicated that the venous/venous capillary ECs in C9 were highly modified by Pdcd10 deletion, while the arterial ECs in C8 were essentially not affected (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Arterial-capillary endothelial cells of C3 and C5 were minimally affected by Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Also, the arterial- capillary ECs of C3 and C5 were minimally affected by Pdcd10 deletion (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Tip cell clusters C1 and C6 and mitotic/venous capillary C7 and capillary C0 Pdcd10-ko endothelial cell clusters showed strong modifications to their gene expression.
source: Furthermore, this analysis also showed that the tip cell C1 and C6 and the mitotic/venous capillary C7 and capillary C0 Pdcd10-ko EC clusters showed strong modifications to their gene expression, which indicated that Pdcd10 deletion was particularly significant in these cells, as compared to the other cell clusters.
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Klf4 and Klf2 are key drivers of the Pdcd10-ko phenotype and are up-regulated in brain endothelial cells after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: The transcription factors Klf4 and Klf2 are key drivers of the Pdcd10-ko phenotype, and they are up-regulated in brain ECs after Pdcd10 deletion (Maddaluno et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2016; Cuttano et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Both Klf4 and Klf2 were up-regulated in Pdcd10-ko endothelial cells compared to Pdcd10-wt endothelial cells in almost all clusters (C0-C7, C9).
source: Here, both Klf4 and Klf2 were up-regulated in the Pdcd10-ko ECs compared to the Pdcd10-wt ECs in almost all of the clusters (C0–C7, C9).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Arterial C8 endothelial cells were not affected by Pdcd10 deletion in terms of Klf4 and Klf2 expression.
source: The exceptions here were the arterial C8 ECs, which were not affected (further commented below), and the tip/capillary C12 and C14 ECs, which showed significant up-regulation of only Klf2 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Tip/capillary C12 and C14 endothelial cells showed significant up-regulation of only Klf2 after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: The exceptions here were the arterial C8 ECs, which were not affected (further commented below), and the tip/capillary C12 and C14 ECs, which showed significant up-regulation of only Klf2 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The greatest up-regulation of Klf4 and Klf2 was seen for tip cell clusters C1 and C6.
source: The greatest up-regulation of Klf4 and Klf2 was seen for the tip cell clusters C1 and C6.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Pdcd10-wt arterial endothelial cells of C8 showed significantly higher expression of Klf4 and Klf2 compared with Pdcd10-wt endothelial cells of all other clusters.
source: Pdcd10-wt arterial ECs of C8 showed significantly higher expression of Klf4 and Klf2 compared with Pdcd10-wt ECs of all the other clusters (average logFC, 0.72, 0.55, respectively; padj <0.05 for both), and there were no differences in Klf4 or Klf2 expression between the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko ECs.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis with statistical significance.

claim: There were no differences in Klf4 or Klf2 expression between Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko arterial C8 endothelial cells.
source: Pdcd10-wt arterial ECs of C8 showed significantly higher expression of Klf4 and Klf2 compared with Pdcd10-wt ECs of all the other clusters (average logFC, 0.72, 0.55, respectively; padj <0.05 for both), and there were no differences in Klf4 or Klf2 expression between the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko ECs.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Pdcd10-ko venous/venous capillary C9 endothelial cells showed up-regulation of most lesion-marker genes.
source: For the Pdcd10-ko, the venous/venous capillary C9 ECs showed up-regulation of most of the lesion-marker genes, followed by the mitotic/venous capillary C7 and tip cell C1 and C6 ECs.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis of lesion markers.

claim: Differentially expressed genes from cluster C9 showed the greatest overlap with the CCM gene set (12 of 51 CCM genes).
source: Here, the DEGs from cluster C9 showed the greatest overlap with the CCM gene set (12 of 51 CCM genes) (Figure 2D; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This statement is based on enrichment analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The venous/venous capillary C9 endothelial cell cluster is the strongest candidate cell cluster for contributions to the most advanced lesion development after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Once again, these observations strongly support the hypothesis that the venous/venous capillary C9 EC cluster is the strongest candidate cell cluster for contributions to the most advanced lesion development after Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on multiple lines of evidence from gene expression and enrichment analyses.

claim: In the absence of Pdcd10 in venous/venous capillary C9 and tip cell C1 and C6 endothelial cells, biological processes implicated in CCM pathology were mainly altered, including angiogenesis, cell differentiation, coagulation, immune responses, and cell apoptosis.
source: In the absence of Pdcd10 in the venous/venous capillary C9 and tip cell C1 and C6 ECs, the biological processes implicated in CCM pathology were mainly altered, which included angiogenesis, cell differentiation, coagulation, immune responses, and cell apoptosis (Figure 2E; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This statement is based on gene set enrichment analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Endothelial cells undergo endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition mediated through increased TGFβ signaling in CCM.
source: In a previous study, we reported that ECs undergo endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition that is mediated through increased TGFβ signaling (Maddaluno et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition is relevant for the development of vascular lesions in CCM.
source: This process is relevant for the development of vascular lesions, and is further confirmed here by this single-cell analysis (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This statement is based on the current single-cell analysis data.

claim: In patients with CCM, the blood-brain barrier is impaired.
source: In patients with CCM, the BBB is impaired (Clatterbuck, 2001; Mikati et al., 2015), as reported here in this murine Pdcd10-depletion model, where there was significant increase in vascular permeability to endogenous immunoglobulins (Figure 2F, cerebellum; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, cerebrum).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research and confirmed by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The murine Pdcd10-depletion model showed significant increase in vascular permeability to endogenous immunoglobulins.
source: In patients with CCM, the BBB is impaired (Clatterbuck, 2001; Mikati et al., 2015), as reported here in this murine Pdcd10-depletion model, where there was significant increase in vascular permeability to endogenous immunoglobulins (Figure 2F, cerebellum; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, cerebrum).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Expression levels of many regulators of BBB formation and maturation were decreased in the potential lesion-forming C9 and C6 clusters.
source: Coherent with this, the expression levels of many regulators of BBB formation and maturation that cooperate to establish the BBB (e.g. Foxf2, Foxq1, Ppard, Zic3) (Hupe et al., 2017) were decreased in the potential lesion-forming C9 and C6 clusters (Figure 2G, pink).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by a citation.

claim: BBB transporters were diffusely down-regulated in Pdcd10-ko cells, with C9, C6, and C7 endothelial cells as the most affected.
source: Transporters that finely tune BBB functions (Figure 2G, green) were also diffusely down-regulated in the Pdcd10-ko cells, with the C9, C6, and C7 ECs as the most affected.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Three transporters (Slc2a1/Glut1, Slc9a3r2, Slc6a6) were all up-regulated in Pdcd10-ko cells of C1, C6, C7, C9, and C12 endothelial cells.
source: Of note, three transporters (i.e. Slc2a1 or Glut1, Slc9a3r2, Slc6a6) were all up-regulated in the Pdcd10-ko cells of the C1, C6, C7, C9, and C12 ECs.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Enhancement of glucose transport mediated by Slc2a1 supports glycolytic metabolism in endothelial cells of tumor vessels.
source: Interestingly, enhancement of glucose transport mediated by Slc2a1 supports glycolytic metabolism in ECs of tumor vessels (Rohlenova et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Arterial C8 Pdcd10-ko endothelial cells and putative arterial-capillary C3 and C5 endothelial cells were minimally or not modified by Pdcd10 deletion.
source: All of these functions indicated were minimally or not modified in the arterial C8 Pdcd10-ko ECs (Figure 2A–G) and in the putative arterial-capillary C3 and C5 ECs (Figure 1J), which were only partially affected by the Pdcd10 deletion (Figure 2A–G).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in multiple figures.

claim: Only Cldn5 expression was down-regulated in C1, C6, and C9 endothelial cells among junctional molecules investigated.
source: Among the panel of junctional molecules investigated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), only Cldn5 expression was down-regulated in the C1, C6, and C9 ECs.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Little or no changes were seen for the expression of other adherens and tight-junction components in Pdcd10-ko endothelial cells.
source: Little or no changes were seen for the expression of other adherens and tight-junction components (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Tight-junction proteins Claudin-5 and Cingulin, as well as adherens junction VE-cadherin, were not correctly localized at cell-to-cell contacts in endothelial cells of cavernomas in Pdcd10-ko mice.
source: However, the tight-junction proteins Claudin-5, and Cingulin, as well as the adherens junction VE-cadherin were not correctly localized at the cell-to-cell contacts in the ECs of the cavernomas of the Pdcd10-ko mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data shown in figures.

claim: Four endothelial subpopulations are particularly affected by Pdcd10 gene deletion: venous/venous capillary C9, tip cell C1 and C6, and mitotic/venous capillary C7 endothelial cell clusters.
source: In summary here, we have identified four endothelial subpopulations that are particularly affected by the deletion of the Pdcd10 gene: the venous/venous capillary C9, tip cell C1 and C6, and mitotic/venous capillary C7 EC clusters.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on multiple lines of evidence from gene expression analyses.

claim: Under Pdcd10-ko conditions, venous/venous capillary C9 endothelial cells represent the strongest candidate to form the most advanced lesions or most progressed lesion areas.
source: Among these, under the Pdcd10-ko conditions here, the venous/venous capillary C9 ECs represent the strongest candidate to form the most advanced lesions, or the most progressed lesion areas.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on multiple lines of evidence from gene expression analyses.

claim: The venous nature of endothelial cells in cavernomas was confirmed by expression of the venous marker COUP-TFII in vivo in CCM lesions.
source: The venous nature of the ECs in the cavernomas was further confirmed by expression of the venous marker COUP-TFII in vivo in the CCM lesions. Figure 2H shows the ECs in a large cavernoma that can be seen to be strongly positive for the venous marker COUP-TFII, which is encoded by Nr2f2.
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data shown in a figure.

claim: Endothelial cells in a large cavernoma are strongly positive for the venous marker COUP-TFII (encoded by Nr2f2).
source: Figure 2H shows the ECs in a large cavernoma that can be seen to be strongly positive for the venous marker COUP-TFII, which is encoded by Nr2f2.
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data shown in a figure.

claim: Despite successful deletion of the Pdcd10 gene, gene expression of arterial endothelial cells (C8) in Pdcd10-ko mice was almost unchanged from the effects of Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Despite the successful deletion of the Pdcd10 gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D), gene expression of the arterial ECs (C8) in the Pdcd10-ko mice was almost unchanged from the effects of Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Arterial C8 endothelial cells showed the lowest total number of differentially expressed genes in comparison of Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko mice.
source: Indeed, in the comparison of the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko mice, these arterial ECs showed the following: the lowest total number of DEGs (Figure 2A); no increase in Klf4 and Klf2 expression (Figure 2B); no, or minimal, signs of increased expression of lesion markers (Figure 2C–E); and no, or minimal, decreases in BBB markers and BBB transporters (Figure 2G).
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: 111 unique marker genes were identified for the arterial C8 cluster with specificity average logFC >0.25 and padj <0.05.
source: Therefore, to investigate the features of these arterial ECs that might promote their refractoriness to lesion formation, we identified the unique marker genes that were expressed in this C8 cluster (threshold: specificity average logFC >0.25; padj <0.05) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis with specified statistical thresholds.

claim: Out of 111 unique marker genes highly expressed in C8 endothelial cell cluster, 80 had potential preventive functions, 5 had potential promotive functions, and 13 had potential dual functions.
source: Out of a total of 111 unique marker genes that were highly expressed in the C8 EC cluster, 80 had potential preventive functions, five had potential promotive functions, and 13 had potential dual functions, which depended on the cellular context (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This statement is based on functional annotation of unique marker genes shown in figures.

claim: Four regulators of DNA remodeling (Chd3, Gadd45g, Hey1, Mapk3) and 10 transcriptional factors were uniquely up-regulated in arterial C8 endothelial cells.
source: These specific functions of the C8 cluster might also be supported by the group of four regulators of DNA remodeling (i.e. Chd3, Gadd45g, Hey1, Mapk3) and 10 transcriptional factors (Gata2, Lmo7, Mecom, Msx1, Notch1, Notch4, Smad7, Sox13, Sox17, Sox18) that were uniquely up-regulated in these arterial C8 ECs (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The levels of expression of Klf2 and Klf4 do not directly correlate with resistance to Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Notably, the levels of expression of Klf2 and Klf4 do not directly correlate with the resistance to Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that arterial C8 cells have high Klf2/Klf4 but are resistant to Pdcd10 deletion.

claim: High levels of Klf2/Klf4 are not sufficient per se to trigger the Pdcd10 phenotype.
source: This suggests that high levels of Klf2/Klf4 are not sufficient per se to trigger the Pdcd10 phenotype.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that arterial C8 cells have high Klf2/Klf4 but do not develop the Pdcd10 phenotype.

claim: Arterial endothelial cells selectively express genes that positively regulate processes altered after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Taken together, it appears that these arterial ECs selectively express genes that positively regulate processes that are altered after the Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the functional annotation of unique marker genes in arterial C8 cells.

claim: Genes expressed in arterial endothelial cells can counteract the effects of Pdcd10 deletion and prevent lesion formation.
source: We hypothesize that these genes can counteract the effects of the Pdcd10 deletion, and thus prevent lesion formation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation that arterial cells express putative preventive genes and are resistant to lesion formation.

claim: The number of Pdcd10-ko cells was significantly increased over respective Pdcd10-wt cells for C9 (4.8-fold), C12 (4.0-fold), and C14 (2.8-fold).
source: The number of Pdcd10-ko cells was significantly increased over the respective Pdcd10-wt cells for C9 (4.8-fold), C12 (4.0-fold), and C14 (2.8-fold) (Figure 1E,F; Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is based on quantitative analysis of cell numbers shown in figures.

claim: Cluster 9 enrichment in Pdcd10-ko cells is likely due to sustained proliferation.
source: Cluster nine enrichment in the Pdcd10-ko cells is likely due to sustained proliferation, as indicated by the greater proportion of the Pdcd10-ko cells (vs. Pdcd10-wt) that expressed mitotic markers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on analysis of mitotic marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 expressed significantly higher levels of several mitotic markers that regulate different phases of mitosis.
source: Furthermore, Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 expressed significantly higher levels of several mitotic markers that regulate different phases of mitosis (Figure 4C), including: G2/M (Ccnb2); mitotic spindle orientation (Cenpa); sister chromatid segregation (Top2a); and exit from mitosis (Ube2s, Ube2c, Birc5) (see references in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by references.

claim: Increased numbers of mitotic endothelial cells (co-expressing Ki-67 and ERG) were seen in cavernomas but not in pseudo-normal vessels of Pdcd10-ko brain.
source: Accordingly, increased numbers of mitotic ECs (i.e. co-expression of Ki-67 and ERG Birdsey et al., 2015; Booth and Earnshaw, 2017) were seen for cavernomas, but not in the pseudo-normal vessels of the Pdcd10-ko brain (Figure 4D, representative immunofluorescence; Figure 4E, quantification; Video 1).
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data and quantification shown in figures and video, supported by citations.

claim: Visium analysis confirmed enhanced proliferation specifically in endothelial cells of cavernomas.
source: This analysis of the Visium data confirmed enhanced proliferation specifically in the ECs of the cavernomas (Figure 4F,G).
evidence: This statement is based on spatial transcriptomics data shown in figures.

claim: Increased proportions of Pdcd10-ko cells expressed tip cell markers (Plaur, Apln, Mmrn2) in C9 and Plaur in C12.
source: For the tip cell traits, as the other crucial phenotype in angiogenesis, increased proportions of the Pdcd10-ko cells expressed a set of tip cell markers in C9 (i.e. Plaur, Apln, Mmrn2) and C12 (i.e. Plaur) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Tip cell clusters C1 and C6 showed the greatest number of up-regulated tip cell markers.
source: While tip cell clusters C1 and C6 showed the greatest number of up-regulated tip cell markers (Figure 5B), C9 Pdcd10-ko cells showed up-regulated expression of only a few tip cell markers (Figure 5B, Mcam, Apln, Plaur).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: C9 Pdcd10-ko cells showed up-regulation of a large set of tumor tip cell markers, which were less modified in C1 and C6.
source: Conversely, C9 Pdcd10-ko cells showed up-regulation of a large set of tumor tip cell markers (Zhao et al., 2018), which were less modified in C1 and C6 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by a citation.

claim: uPAR (encoded by Plaur) was highly expressed in both overt lesions and pseudo-normal vessels of brains from Pdcd10-ko mice.
source: According to the enhanced expression of the tip cell marker Plaur in the Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 (as well as in various other clusters), uPAR (encoded by Plaur) was highly expressed both in overt lesions and in pseudo-normal vessels of the brains from the Pdcd10-ko mice, as shown in Figure 5D, and quantified in Figure 5E.
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data and quantification shown in figures.

claim: The densities of tip cells were similar in Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko brains when considering both pseudo-normal vessels and cavernomas.
source: However, considering both pseudo-normal vessels and cavernomas, the densities of the tip cells were similar in the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko brains (Figure 5G).
evidence: This statement is based on quantification of tip cells shown in a figure.

claim: Tip cells at the vascular front were significantly denser in retinas from Pdcd10-ko than Pdcd10-wt.
source: The tip cells at the vascular front were significantly denser in the retinas from the Pdcd10-ko than for the Pdcd10-wt (Figure 5H, tip cells at front), while the numbers of filopodia per tip cell were comparable for the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko (Figure 5H, filopodia/cell).
evidence: This statement is based on quantification of tip cells in retina shown in a figure.

claim: The numbers of filopodia per tip cell were comparable for Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko retinas.
source: The tip cells at the vascular front were significantly denser in the retinas from the Pdcd10-ko than for the Pdcd10-wt (Figure 5H, tip cells at front), while the numbers of filopodia per tip cell were comparable for the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko (Figure 5H, filopodia/cell).
evidence: This statement is based on quantification shown in a figure.

claim: About 15 to 30% of Pdcd10-ko tip cells were not extended and appeared blocked within the dense cell layer (tip-like cells).
source: However, the Pdcd10-wt tip cells showed typical elongated cell bodies, while about 15 to 30% of the Pdcd10-ko tip cells were not extended and appeared blocked within the dense cell layer (Figure 5H, tip-like cells).
evidence: This statement is based on morphological analysis and quantification shown in a figure.

claim: Blocked tip-like cells represented only 10% in Pdcd10-wt retinas.
source: Similarly, the blocked tip-like cells only represented 10% in the Pdcd10-wt (Figure 5H, tip-like cells).
evidence: This statement is based on quantification shown in a figure.

claim: Radial expansion of the vascular network was significantly inhibited in Pdcd10-ko retina.
source: Consistent with the impaired tip cell phenotype, radial expansion of the vascular network was significantly inhibited in the Pdcd10-ko retina (Figure 5I, quantification in Figure 5J).
evidence: This statement is based on quantification of radial expansion shown in figures.

claim: In Pdcd10-ko retina, cells with filopodia were present in the walls of veins proximal to the optic nerves, which were never observed in Pdcd10-wt veins in this region.
source: Of particular interest, in the Pdcd10-ko retina, there were cells with filopodia also in the walls of the veins proximal to the optic nerves (Figure 5F, rear, asterisks; Video 2). In this region, the tip cells were never observed in the wall of Pdcd10-wt veins.
evidence: This statement is based on immunofluorescence data shown in a figure and video.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 (venous/venous capillary) are more mitotic than respective Pdcd10-wt cells.
source: All in all, these data indicate that the Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 (i.e. venous/venous capillary) are more mitotic than the respective Pdcd10-wt cells.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on multiple lines of evidence about mitotic marker expression and proliferation.

claim: Tip cell traits were expressed in Pdcd10-ko cells of C9, although they did not show a normal profile.
source: Tip cell traits were also expressed in the Pdcd10-ko cells of C9, although they did not show a normal profile.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on tip cell marker expression and morphological analysis.

claim: 15 to 30% of lesion endothelial cell-containing spots were positive for both tip cell and mitotic-cell markers according to Visium analysis.
source: These data were also validated using the Visium analysis, where 15 to 30% of the lesion ECs contained spots that were positive for both tip cell and mitotic-cell markers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This statement is based on spatial transcriptomics data shown in figures.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells in C9 develop aberrant tip cell and mitotic characters.
source: These data thus support the model that the Pdcd10-ko cells in C9 develop aberrant tip cell and mitotic characters, while the Pdcd10-ko cells in the other clusters mainly acquire abnormal tip cell traits.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on multiple lines of evidence about tip cell and mitotic marker expression.

claim: The angiogenic (tip cell/mitotic) phenotype in Pdcd10-ko cells is defective, as network elongation is impaired and cell proliferation is enhanced.
source: This angiogenic (tip cell/mitotic) phenotype is, indeed, defective, as network elongation is impaired, and cell proliferation is enhanced.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on observations of impaired radial expansion and increased proliferation.

claim: The combination of high cell proliferation and low cell motility might explain the formation of cavernomas.
source: The combination of high cell proliferation and low cell motility might explain the formation of the cavernomas (see also Castro et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of cavernoma formation, supported by a citation.

claim: STREAM was used to infer a trajectory structure that recapitulated endothelial lineage differentiation during vascular development.
source: Using both Pdcd10-ko and Pdcd10-wt data, Single-cell Trajectories Reconstruction, Exploration and Mapping (STREAM) (Chen et al., 2019) was used to infer a trajectory structure that recapitulated the endothelial lineage differentiation during vascular development, with tip cells (C1, C6) defined on branches S4–S3 and S5–S3, respectively (Figure 6A), and venous/venous capillary (C9) and mitotic/capillary (C7) cells on branches S0–S2 and S0–S1 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement describes the computational method used for trajectory analysis and its results, supported by a citation and figures.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells of Cluster 9 were distributed over different branches of the trajectory (S3-S0, S0-S2, S0-S1).
source: Pdcd10-ko cells of cluster 9 were distributed over different branches of the trajectory (S3–S0, S0–S2, S0–S1), as shown in Figure 6B,C.
evidence: This statement is based on trajectory analysis shown in figures.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells of C9 in the S0-S2 branch highly expressed typical cavernoma markers, were mainly mitotic, and had pathological tip cell traits.
source: In summary here, the C9 Pdcd10-ko cells in the newly formed Pdcd10-ko specific branch of S0–S2 highly expressed typical cavernoma markers, they were mainly mitotic, and they also had pathological tip cell traits.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on trajectory analysis and gene expression patterns.

claim: C9 Pdcd10-ko cells in the S0-S2 branch can be envisaged as endothelial cells of typical cavernoma lesions.
source: All in all, these can be envisaged as ECs of typical cavernoma lesions.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the characteristics of cells in the S0-S2 branch.

claim: Pdcd10-ko cells for S0-S2 versus S0-S1 showed increased expression of the transcriptional stimulator Tcf15.
source: The Pdcd10-ko cells for S0–S2 versus S0–S1 showed increased expression of the transcriptional stimulator of progenitor cell proliferation and differentiation, Tcf15 (Davies et al., 2013; Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This statement is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by a citation.

claim: Id1 was up-regulated in Pdcd10-ko endothelial cells of lesions and was strongly increased in the S0-S2 branch.
source: As previously reported (Maddaluno et al., 2013), Id1 was up-regulated in Pdcd10-ko ECs of lesions, and it was consistently strongly increased in the S0–S2 branch (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Id1 inhibits Tcf15-mediated progenitor cell differentiation but not Tcf15-mediated proliferation of progenitor cells.
source: Remarkably, Id1 inhibits Tcf15-mediated progenitor cell differentiation, but not Tcf15-mediated proliferation of progenitor cells (Davies et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Cavernomas have clonal origins from expansion of Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells.
source: Considering that our group recently reported that cavernomas have clonal origins from expansion of Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells (Malinverno et al., 2019), we investigated the distribution of cells that expressed progenitor cell markers in the STREAM-generated trajectories.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: The proportions of Pdcd10-ko cells positive for Bst1 or Peg3 were highly and specifically increased in the S0-S2 and S3-S0 branches.
source: The proportions of Pdcd10-ko cells that were positive for Bst1 or Peg3 were highly, and specifically, increased in the S0–S2 and S3–S0 branches (Figure 6E, arrows).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression in trajectory branches shown in a figure.

claim: The proportions of Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko cells positive for Procr and Cd200 were similar across all branches of the trajectory.
source: In contrast, the proportions of Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko cells positive for Procr and Cd200 were similar across all of the branches of the trajectory (Figure 6E, lower panels).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: Co-expression of progenitor cell markers and Mki67 in Pdcd10-wt cells was limited to cells in the S0-S1 branch.
source: As shown in Figure 6F, co-expression of progenitor cell markers and Mki67 in Pdcd10-wt cells was limited to the cells in the S0–S1 branch (orange bars), where mitotic C7 cells were located (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of co-expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: There were increased proportions of Mki67-positive Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells in all branches, with the strongest increases in S0-S2.
source: Conversely, there were increased proportions of Mki67-positive Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells in all of the branches, with the strongest increases seen for S0–S2 (Figure 6F, blue bars), compared to the Pdcd10-wt.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of co-expression patterns shown in a figure.

claim: Expression levels of Bst1 were specifically high in Pdcd10-ko cells of the S0-S2 branch.
source: Moreover, the expression levels of Bst1 were specifically high in the Pdcd10-ko cells of the S0–S2 branch, while the expression of the other progenitor cell markers in the Pdcd10-ko cells was high, but more similar across all of the branches of the trajectory (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Id1 expression was high in Bst1-positive cells in the S0-S2 branch, suggesting that differentiation in these resident progenitor cells can be inhibited.
source: Interestingly, Id1 expression was high in Bst1-positive cells in the S0–S2 branch, which suggested that differentiation in these resident progenitor cells can be inhibited (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C) as mentioned above and shown by Davies et al., 2013.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on gene expression analysis shown in a figure and supported by a citation.

claim: Bst1-positive and Peg3-positive resident endothelial progenitor cells were specifically concentrated in the branches most affected by Pdcd10 deletion.
source: These data indicate that Bst1-positive and Peg3-positive resident endothelial progenitor cells were specifically concentrated in the branches that were most affected by Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on analysis of progenitor marker distribution in trajectory branches.

claim: Klf4 and Klf2 were highly expressed in Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells of the S0-S2 branch that were positive for Bst1, Peg3, Procr, and Cd200.
source: Interestingly, the key driver genes of the CCM phenotype, Klf4 and Klf2, were highly expressed in Pdcd10-ko progenitor cells of the S0–S2 branch that were also positive for Bst1, Peg3, Procr, and Cd200, and also for these cells of the other branches (Figure 6G; Figure 6—figure supplement 2D, respectively).
evidence: This statement is based on gene expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: Klf4 and Klf2 are early response genes to Pdcd10 deletion in resident endothelial progenitor cells.
source: This supports the concept that Klf4 and Klf2 are early response genes to Pdcd10 deletion in these types of resident endothelial progenitor cells.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that Klf4 and Klf2 are highly expressed in progenitor cells.

claim: Colocalization of Bst1 and cavernoma transcripts (Klf2, Klf4, Ly6a) using Visium showed concentration of Bst1 progenitor cell transcripts at the level of cavernomas and mulberry lesions.
source: Colocalization of Bst1 and the cavernoma transcripts Klf2, Klf4, and Ly6a using Visium (Figure 7A,B) showed concentration of Bst1 progenitor cell transcripts at the level of cavernomas and mulberry lesions (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement is based on spatial transcriptomics data shown in figures.

claim: The presence of Bst1-positive cells in lesions was confirmed through in-situ hybridization in brain sections of Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko.
source: Similarly, we also confirmed the presence of Bst1-positive cells in the lesions through in-situ hybridization in brain sections of the Pdcd10-wt and Pdcd10-ko (Figure 7C; Malinverno et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is based on in-situ hybridization data shown in a figure and supported by a citation.

claim: After Pdcd10 deletion, the proportions of Bst1-positive cells increased in all capillary-vein clusters (C2, C4, C7), with greatest expression in venous/venous capillary C9 (39.9%).
source: In the analysis of the clusters identified in this scRNA-seq analysis, after Pdcd10 deletion the proportions of Bst1-positive cells increased in all of the capillary-vein clusters (C2, C4, C7), with the greatest expression in the venous/venous capillary C9 (Figure 7D; Bst1-positive cells, 39.9%), which is in agreement with the data reported in Figure 6E.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: The proportions of Bst1-positive cells did not increase in arterial C8 and arterial capillary C3 and C5 Pdcd10-ko cells compared to respective Pdcd10-wt.
source: In contrast, the proportions of Bst1-positive cells did not increase in only the arterial C8 and arterial capillary C3 and C5 Pdcd10-ko cells, in comparison with the respective Pdcd10-wt (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: Bst1 appears to be a preferential physiological marker of vein-resident progenitor cells that is particularly increased in venous clusters after Pdcd10 deletion, with no increase in arterial clusters.
source: Therefore, Bst1 appears to be a preferential physiological marker of vein-resident progenitor cells that is particularly increased in venous clusters after Pdcd10 deletion, with no increase in arterial clusters (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the differential expression pattern of Bst1 in venous versus arterial clusters.

claim: Peg3 showed highest expression in venous C9 Pdcd10-ko cells (24.0% vs. 9.3% in wt).
source: Although Peg3 appears to be a more general marker of resident endothelial progenitor cells in Pdcd10-wt cells, it showed highest expression in venous C9 Pdcd10-ko cells (Peg3-positive cells vs. wt, 24.0% vs. 9.3%).
evidence: This statement is based on quantitative analysis of progenitor marker expression.

claim: Venous-capillary C7 Pdcd10-ko cells showed the second highest increase in Peg3 expression.
source: The venous-capillary C7 Pdcd10-ko cells showed the second highest increase (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: The proportions of Peg3-positive cells did not increase in any of the artery and arterial capillary clusters after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: As for Bst1, the proportions of Peg3-positive cells did not increase in any of the artery and arterial capillary clusters, which suggests that Pdcd10 deletion can induce endothelial proliferation at different maturation stages.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression and includes an inference about proliferation.

claim: Procr-positive and Cd200-positive cells were ubiquitously expressed in Pdcd10-wt venous and arterial clusters and did not significantly increase after Pdcd10 deletion at the developmental stage examined (8dpn).
source: The Procr-positive and Cd200-positive cells (Figure 7D) were ubiquitously expressed in the Pdcd10-wt venous and arterial clusters, and did not significantly increase after Pdcd10 deletion at the developmental stage examined (8dpn), in agreement with the trajectory data of Figure 6E.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression shown in a figure.

claim: Brain endothelial cells represent a heterogeneous population distributed across 13 different clusters based on gene expression.
source: Through single-cell transcriptomic analysis, we have identified here some unique characteristics of ECs that form either normal vessels or cavernomas. Here, we have shown that brain ECs represent a heterogeneous population that is distributed across 13 different clusters on the basis of their gene expression.
evidence: This statement is a summary of the single-cell RNA sequencing results.

claim: Brain endothelial cells express highly specialized functions that help form vasculature appropriate for brain vascularization and blood-brain barrier development.
source: These cells express highly specialized functions that help to form the vasculature that is most appropriate for the needs of brain vascularization and for the development of the BBB (Figures 1I and 8A).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the analysis of specialized gene expression patterns shown in figures.

claim: Resident progenitor cells were detected in all Pdcd10-wt clusters, although in different proportions.
source: Remarkably, resident progenitor cells were detected in all of the Pdcd10-wt clusters, although in different proportions.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of progenitor marker expression across clusters.

claim: Resident progenitor cells are heterogeneous and share several transcriptional features with endothelial cells of the vessels where they reside.
source: This indicates that resident progenitor cells are heterogeneous and share several transcriptional features with the ECs of the vessels where they reside (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that progenitor cells are found in different clusters with different characteristics.

claim: The 'progenitor' status might represent a transient and reversible response to microenvironmental signals rather than a fate-committed, stable identity.
source: It can be speculated that this 'mimicry' behavior of endothelial-resident progenitors might be determined by the specificity of the different vascular microenvironments, and even that the 'progenitor' status might represent a transient and reversible response to microenvironmental signals, rather than a fate-committed, stable identity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the nature of progenitor cell identity.

claim: Although Pdcd10 deletion takes place comparably in arterial and venous endothelial cells, only venous endothelial cells can respond to Pdcd10 deletion.
source: Although Pdcd10 deletion takes place comparably in arterial and venous ECs, only venous ECs can respond to Pdcd10 deletion.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on the differential response of arterial versus venous cells to Pdcd10 deletion.

claim: Pdcd10-ko venous cells follow defective differentiation and angiogenic programs with abnormal tip cell traits and increased mitosis, giving rise to cavernous branching and mulberry lesions.
source: Pdcd10-ko venous cells follow defective differentiation and angiogenic programs, with abnormal tip cell traits and increased mitosis, giving rise to cavernous branching and mulberry lesions.
evidence: This statement is a summary inference based on multiple lines of evidence about venous cell behavior after Pdcd10 deletion.

claim: The venous compartment responds to Pdcd10 deletion with increased numbers and expression levels of venous resident endothelial cell progenitors.
source: Moreover, the venous compartment responds to Pdcd10 deletion with increased numbers and expression levels of venous resident endothelial cell progenitors.
evidence: This statement is a summary of findings about progenitor cell responses to Pdcd10 deletion.

claim: The trigger in cavernoma formation is the recruitment of progenitor cells that attract mature endothelial cells into the areas of the lesions.
source: These observations confirm our previous study (Malinverno et al., 2019), where we showed that the trigger in cavernoma formation is the recruitment of progenitor cells that attract mature ECs into the areas of the lesions.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: Goveia et al. recently described Bst1-positive cells as vein-resident endothelial stem cells with unexplored roles in lung tumor vascularization.
source: Interestingly, Goveia et al. recently described Bst1-positive cells as vein-resident endothelial stem cells that still have unexplored roles in lung tumor vascularization (Goveia et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to recent research.

claim: The same mutation and inactivation of Pdcd10 can result in strongly different responses in endothelial cells of venous and arterial origin, and in resident progenitor cells.
source: Thus, the same mutation and inactivation of Pdcd10 can result in strongly different responses in ECs of venous and arterial origin, and in the resident progenitor cells.
evidence: This statement is a summary conclusion based on the differential responses observed across cell types.

claim: While Klf2 and Klf4 are necessary for expression of the mutant phenotype, they are not sufficient.
source: This indicates that while Klf2 and Klf4 are necessary for expression of the mutant phenotype (Zhou et al., 2016; Cuttano et al., 2016), they are not sufficient.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that Klf2/Klf4 expression doesn't correlate with phenotype severity, supported by citations.

claim: A specific transcriptional landscape appears necessary to allow the full transformation after Pdcd10 deletion.
source: A specific transcriptional landscape appears necessary to allow the full transformation.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that Klf2/Klf4 alone are not sufficient for transformation.

claim: This study identifies venous endothelial cell clusters and their related progenitor cells as the main cell types responsible for cavernoma development.
source: Overall, this study adds several new aspects to the evolution of CCM and identifies the venous EC clusters and their related progenitor cells as the main cell types responsible for cavernoma development.
evidence: This statement is a summary conclusion based on the integrated analysis of multiple data types.
